evidence.why: Separate damage and eligible-count updates, including the zero-pair-count test.
Victim pair counts are cleared without resetting attacker aggregates.

facts.rationale: The previous distinct-opponent description ignored the independently reset victim-owned pair counter.
facts.value: Records attributed attacker-versus-victim hit observations. Unless the victim discriminator equals 1, it stores the attacker's latest victim and damage and accumulates victim-owned per-attacker damage. For attack codes outside the five excluded classes, it also increments the attacker's eligible-hit count and the pair hit count; the attacker's xC increments when that pair count was zero. xC therefore counts first-counted-hit events across victim-history reset intervals, not globally distinct opponent slots.

evidence.why: Pair reset permits repeated first-hit qualification for the same victim.

facts.rationale: Preserves the exact filters while correcting the cross-record lifetime interpretation.
facts.value: Victim discriminator 1 suppresses every update. Otherwise latest victim, latest damage, and accumulated pair damage are always updated. Codes 0x4C, 0x5A, 0x5B, 0x5C, and 0x60 suppress only ordinary hit-count updates. Other codes increment attacker x8, increment attacker xC if victim.x10[attacker].x4 was zero, and then increment that pair count. A later pl_800411C4 reset can make the same victim contribute another xC increment; xC is not a lifetime uniqueness count.

facts.rationale: Corrects the unsupported interpretation as an average over globally distinct opponents.
facts.value: Returns the selected player's accumulated eligible-hit count x8 divided by its accumulated first-counted-hit-event count xC, with a zero result when xC is zero. A first-counted-hit event occurs when an eligible hit finds the victim-owned pair count at zero; independent victim-history resets allow the same opponent to contribute more than once.

evidence.why: Separate reset and exact getter signature.

facts.rationale: Preserves the signature while correcting both counter-domain precision and the denominator's lifetime.
facts.value: Read-only getter with signature float(int player_slot). It reads the u32 aggregate counters pl_x5EC_t.x8 and xC and returns their floating-point ratio. x8 counts eligible hits; xC counts eligible hits that encountered a zero victim-owned pair count, including renewed first hits after that victim's history resets.

evidence.why: Transient reset does not clear aggregates.

facts.rationale: Retains the exact two result paths without the erroneous distinct-opponent label.
facts.value: Does not mutate either counter. If xC is nonzero it returns (f32)x8 / xC; otherwise it returns 0.0F. These aggregate counters survive the transient victim-entry reset in pl_800411C4, so the denominator is not a count of currently populated entries or globally unique opponents.

facts.rationale: The consumer remains supported; the statistic is not an average over globally distinct opponent slots.
facts.value: Supplies a combat-history ratio used by the general bonus evaluator: accumulated eligible hits divided by accumulated first-counted-hit events across victim-history intervals. When the returned ratio reaches pl_804D6470->x0, the consumer sets indexed bonus flag 1. The displayed bonus name is not established here.

evidence.why: True assignment on hit, raw assignment on miss, and literal wrapper modes.
Unsigned byte count and unsigned one-bit flag.

facts.rationale: The previous account missed the hit-versus-insertion assignment difference and finite byte-count behavior.
facts.value: Key zero causes no history mutation. A matching key leaves the cursor unchanged: nonzero mode sets its flag to true, while zero mode increments its u8 count modulo 256. A missing key first evaluates the cursor-selected old count and flag, then replaces the entry. Zero mode inserts count 1 and flag 0. Nonzero mode inserts count 0 and assigns the raw mode to the unsigned one-bit flag, retaining its low bit rather than normalizing every nonzero value to true. The cursor wraps from 4 to 0. The two local wrappers pass only literal modes 0 and 1.

evidence.why: u16 API inputs compared with and stored into x8D8 entries.

facts.rationale: Corrects the prior claim that x8D8 physically stores 16-bit identifiers and records useful actual widths without asserting compiled layout.
facts.value: C module operating on three embedded player-owned records: pl_x5EC_t has aggregate fields and six pair entries, including floating-point damage, signed 16-bit hit/sequence counters, an int code, and a one-bit flag; pl_x8C0_t has an int cursor and five entries with u16 keys, u8 counts, and one-bit flags; pl_x8D8_t has an int cursor and five entries with u32 stored identifiers and two one-bit flags. The x8D8 registration and marking APIs accept u16 identifiers, so input narrowing is distinct from storage width. Qualifying records feed indexed point-bonus assignment or increment operations.

evidence.why: Identifier forwarded to count or flag wrapper.
Wrappers forward the key unchanged and updater rejects zero.

facts.rationale: Adds useful missing key-domain knowledge and prevents interpreting the final-hit history as aggregation by move class.
facts.value: u16 final-hit attack-instance identifier, with zero ignored by the history updater. In the demonstrated event path it originates from ft_8008989C, which returns Fighter.dmg.x18ec_instancehitby; it is not the attack-class byte used by the repeated-attack tracker.

evidence.why: BombHei collision path and victim/instance arguments.
Unrestricted matching marker and later disqualification predicate.

facts.rationale: Adds the independently demonstrated gameplay origin of the otherwise generic all-matching marker, without inventing the displayed bonus name.
facts.value: Marks the selected victim player's retained Bob-omb history when canonical item collision processing reports a BombHei instance. The caller supplies the victim player ID and the item's instance identifier narrowed to u16. Marked valid entries subsequently fail the valid-and-unmarked condition for decision 0xC8; this routine does not itself award a bonus, clear entries, or require that a matching entry be valid.
